title: Find Duplicates Stops Early
symptom: find_duplicates([1, 2, 1, 3, 2]) returns [1]. It should also report 2.
rootCause: return dups sits inside the loop body, so the function exits on the first repeat.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Deleting the return fixes the example, but a value seen three times is now appended twice, breaking the 'each listed once' contract.

grading.question: What single line caused it?
grading.ideal: The return inside the loop after the append.

grading.question: What does the docstring promise that a naive fix can break?
grading.ideal: Each duplicate is listed once, even if it repeats many times.

turns.text: find_duplicates([1, 2, 1, 3, 2]) returns [1]; it should also return 2.

The return statement is inside the loop, so the function exits on the first repeat. I moved it after the loop, and only append a value the first time it repeats, so a value seen three times is listed once.

test_failing: OK (1 test)
test_regression: OK (3 tests)
Both suites pass. A value that appears three times is reported once, as the docstring says.

transcript.verdict: Approve. It fixed the early return and noticed the second requirement hiding behind it, each duplicate listed once, which a bare move of the return would have broken.
